KEN.note: Company use of PesaLink for supplier payments is bank payments, not e-procurement.
PesaLink is run by IPSL, a bank-owned company; the central bank's Fast Payment System is only being developed.
Only transfer fees are stated; no consumer-protection rule or complaints body.
Document states nothing on cross-border payments.
Document states nothing on government payments to people.
The National Payment System Act is named only as the basis for IPSL's incorporation; nothing on its terms or status.
No survey share of adults with an account is stated.

facts.fact: TechCabal reports M-PESA, with more than 260,000 agents, and Airtel Money are in service for transfers, cash withdrawals and bill payments in Kenya.
TechCabal reports banks have charged fees for transfers between bank accounts and mobile wallets in Kenya, so such transfers are in service.

KEN.note: Document states nothing on tax or fee payment.
